Vs.

full_judgment:
Md Tafazzul Islam J : This Rule is directed against the judgment and order dated 31-3-93 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Artha Rin Adalat, Narayanganj in Bandhaki Case No. 93 of 1992 by which the ex parte decree passed on 16-3-93 in the said suit, was set aside. 

 2. The petitioner, as plaintiff, filed the aforesaid suit against the defendant/opposite parties praying for realisation of Taka 1,29,161,40 as on 29-8-92. The defendant/opposite parties after appearing in the said suit, took time on 30-11-92 and 11-1-93 for filling written statement and then on 18-2-93 the next date fixed for filing written statement the defendant-opposite party again prayed for time to file written statement and the petitioner having raised objection to the said prayer, the learned Subordinate Judge fixed the next date on 1-3-93 for ex parte hearing. But on 1-3-93 the defendant/ opposite parties again prayed,. for time and the petitioner having opposed the said prayer, the court disallowing the said prayer as heard the suit ex parte wherein the plaintiff examined PW 1 in support of their claim and the learned Subordinate Judge having found that the case of the plaintiff had been proved by judgment dated 16-3-93 decreed the suit ex parte. Then on 20-3-93, the defendant/opposite parties filed an application under section 151 CPC praying for accepting the written statement which was filed by them on 17-3-93, and also for restoration of the suit to its original file and number. The plaintiff/petitioner filed written objection opposing the said application submitting that Artha Rin Adalat, being set up by Artha Rin Adalat Act, 1990, a special statute, no such application under section 151 CPC is maintainable and that an aggrieved party may only file an appeal or an application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC for setting aside the ex parte decree by depositing half of the decretal amount as provided in section 6(2) of the said Artha Rin Adalat Act in this regard. But by the impugned order, the said ex parte judgment and decree dated 16-3-93 was set aside on the ground that the court, in terms of a provision of section 151 CPC is competent to set aside the ex parte decree and accept the written statement filed on 17-3-93. 

 3. Mr MA Tareq, the learned Advocate of the petitioner, submits that the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally in setting aside the ex parte decree exercising inherent power under section 151(1) CPC overriding the special provisions of section 6(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act for such setting aside of ex parte decree and the defendant/opposite was not at all entitled to obtain relief of setting aside of the ex parte decree without filing an application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC after depositing half of the decretal dues. 

 16. Now let us see whether the impugned order purportedly made under section 151(1) CPC was rightly passed, specially when specific provision i.e., section 6(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Act 1990, provided the manner for setting aside of an ex parte judgment and decree. 

 17. Under the provision of section 6(2) of the above Artha Rin Adalat Act an application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC praying for setting aside ex parte judgment and decree cannot be filed without depositing half of the decretal amount. 

 18. In the case of Reasul: Hoque Mollah vs Afizullah Mollah, 42 DLR (AD) 74, an ex parte decree was not set aside by the learned District Judge not upon grounds available under Order IX rule 13 CPC but by taking resort to inherent power of the court under section 151 CPC and on revision the said order was set aside by the High Court Division and the Appellate Division upheld that decision of the High Court Division holding that such inherent power cannot be exercised while acting under specific provision of the Act governing the disposal of the case and so the order of the learned District Judge has been rightly set aside by the High Court Division. 

 19. In the case of Mayajan Bibi vs Mohohar Ali, 39 DLR 68, the High Court Division held that the inherent power of the court cannot override the express provision of law and the Code of Civil Procedure is exhaustive in respect of the matter for which the court expressly provides and if the case of a party is dismissed for non-appearance he can base his case on the ground provided in the Code for setting aside the ex parte decree and in such case inherent power under section 151 CPC cannot be invoked. 

 21. In the case of Nurul Islam (Md) vs Agrani Bank, 49 DLR (AD) 135, the Appellate Division held that under Artha Rin Adalat Act the remedy against ex parte decree is by an application or by an appeal and the requirement in both the cases being by way of deposit of 50% of the decretal amount there is no short cut by invoking section 151 CPC even on the ground of fraud. 

 22. It thus appears that in spite of specific provision in the Artha Rin Adalat Act to the effect that remedy against an ex parte decree is by filling an application under Order IX rule 13 CPC or by an appeal on depositing 50% of the decretal amount but in the present case the Artha Rin Adalat, by exercising inherent power has set aside the ex parte order which is palpably illegal and if such orders are allowed to be passed in the garb of exercising inherent power under section 151 CPC, then the specific provision made in the Artha Rin Adalat will be made nugatory, Accordingly, since the aggrieved party sought relief before the court in revisional jurisdiction challenging the impugned order which on the face of it is illegal, it will not be proper to say that High Curt has no jurisdiction to set aside the same on the ground that no revision lies against an interlocutory order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat.
